tool_input.description: Probe ambiguous DateUtils behaviors to verify assumptions before writing tests
Clean scratch probe files and re-run test suite

result:
Clean — only the compiled test output remains. The only file I created is `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java`.

Summary: I wrote 101 self-contained JUnit 5 tests for `DateUtils` covering add/set/round/truncate/ceiling, fragment calculations, same-day/instant/local-time checks, the day iterator, lenient vs. strict parsing, `toCalendar`/`toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`, `truncatedCompareTo`/`truncatedEquals`, and boundary/error cases (null args, invalid fields/range styles, out-of-range `set*` values, the 280-million-year `ArithmeticException` threshold, iterator exhaustion/`remove()`). All 101 tests pass against the current implementation — I found no genuine code bugs, only a self-contradictory javadoc example in `getFragmentInMinutes` (the "435" example for the `MONTH` fragment ignores the elapsed full days, contradicting both its own prose and the analogous Hours/Seconds/Milliseconds examples); I tested against the correct, day-inclusive value instead and noted this discrepancy in a comment rather than reporting it as a functional bug, since the code itself behaves consistently and correctly.
